<pr_description>
Consider the following PR description:
Cannot drop unique_together constraint on a single field with its own unique=True constraint
Description
	
I have an erroneous unique_together constraint on a model's primary key (unique_together = (('id',),)) that cannot be dropped by a migration. Apparently the migration tries to find all unique constraints on the column and expects there to be only one, but I've got two — the primary key and the unique_together constraint:
Indexes:
	"foo_bar_pkey" PRIMARY KEY, btree (id)
	"foo_bar_id_1c3b3088c74c3b17_uniq" UNIQUE CONSTRAINT, btree (id)
Database is PostgreSQL, if that makes any difference.

</pr_description>

I’ll update the schema editor’s `_delete_composed_index()` to handle cases where multiple constraints exist for the same column(s) (e.g., PK/field-unique plus an erroneous single-column `unique_together`). The fix will disambiguate by preferring the constraint name Django would have generated for the composed index (suffix-based), and otherwise fall back to excluding primary key constraints.

from pathlib import Path
path = Path('django/db/backends/base/schema.py')
text = path.read_text()

new = """            self._delete_composed_index(\n                model,\n                fields,\n                {\"unique\": True},\n                self.sql_delete_unique,\n                suffix=\"_uniq\",\n            )\n"""
if old not in text:
    raise SystemExit('Expected snippet for alter_unique_together not found')
text = text.replace(old, new)
# Update alter_index_together call
old = """            self._delete_composed_index(\n                model,\n                fields,\n                {\"index\": True, \"unique\": False},\n                self.sql_delete_index,\n            )\n"""
new = """            self._delete_composed_index(\n                model,\n                fields,\n                {\"index\": True, \"unique\": False},\n                self.sql_delete_index,\n                suffix=\"_idx\",\n            )\n"""
if old not in text:
    raise SystemExit('Expected snippet for alter_index_together not found')
text = text.replace(old, new)

# Replace _delete_composed_index definition block.
start = text.index('    def _delete_composed_index(')
# find end at next def alter_db_table
end = text.index('\n    def alter_db_table', start)
block = text[start:end]

replacement = '''    def _delete_composed_index(
        self, model, fields, constraint_kwargs, sql, suffix=None
    ):
        meta_constraint_names = {
            constraint.name for constraint in model._meta.constraints
        }
        meta_index_names = {constraint.name for constraint in model._meta.indexes}
        columns = [model._meta.get_field(field).column for field in fields]
        excluded_names = meta_constraint_names | meta_index_names

        identifier_converter = self.connection.introspection.identifier_converter

        def _constraint_name_candidates(constraint_names):
            """Return a narrowed list of matching constraint names.

            Composed indexes created by Django (unique_together/index_together)
            have deterministic names. On some databases, a column may also have
            other unique constraints (e.g. primary key or column-level UNIQUE),
            so multiple matches are possible.
            """
            if not suffix or len(constraint_names) <= 1:
                return constraint_names

            expected_name = identifier_converter(
                self._create_index_name(model._meta.db_table, columns, suffix)
            )
            exact = [
                name
                for name in constraint_names
                if identifier_converter(name) == expected_name
            ]
            if len(exact) == 1:
                return exact

            # As a fallback, try to disambiguate using the expected suffix.
            # This may happen, for example, if the constraint was created under
            # a different table name (e.g. after db_table renames).
            suffix_matches = [
                name
                for name in constraint_names
                if identifier_converter(name).endswith(suffix)
            ]
            if len(suffix_matches) == 1:
                return suffix_matches
            return constraint_names

        constraint_names = self._constraint_names(
            model,
            columns,
            exclude=excluded_names,
            **constraint_kwargs,
        )
        constraint_names = _constraint_name_candidates(constraint_names)

        if len(constraint_names) != 1 and "primary_key" not in constraint_kwargs:
            # Avoid accidentally deleting the primary key if it matches the same
            # columns (e.g. unique_together on a primary key field).
            non_pk_constraint_names = self._constraint_names(
                model,
                columns,
                exclude=excluded_names,
                primary_key=False,
                **constraint_kwargs,
            )
            non_pk_constraint_names = _constraint_name_candidates(
                non_pk_constraint_names
            )
            if len(non_pk_constraint_names) == 1:
                constraint_names = non_pk_constraint_names

        if len(constraint_names) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                "Found wrong number (%s) of constraints for %s(%s)"
                % (
                    len(constraint_names),
                    model._meta.db_table,
                    ", ".join(columns),
                )
            )
        self.execute(self._delete_constraint_sql(sql, model, constraint_names[0]))
'''

text = text[:start] + replacement + text[end:]
path.write_text(text)
print('patched')
